tiny & Tall: Gleipnir – Part One is a point-and-click adventure that offers a fresh and humorous take on Norse mythology while embracing the spirit of classic adventure games. Developed by tT Studios and published by Plug In Digital, it puts players in the shoes of two unlikely blacksmiths tasked with forging the legendary chain Gleipnir, the unbreakable tether meant to restrain the great wolf Fenrir. What makes the game instantly stand out is its commitment to lighthearted storytelling and its hand-drawn presentation, which together create an experience that feels both nostalgic and original.

The narrative follows Tiny and Tall, a mismatched pair of blacksmiths who stumble into an absurd contract with the gods. Their task is seemingly impossible: collect bizarre ingredients like the roots of a mountain, the sound of a cat’s footstep, or the beard of a woman, and use them to craft a chain capable of binding a godlike beast. The absurdity of the quest is central to the charm of the game, as it provides endless opportunities for humor and clever problem-solving. Tiny’s innocent optimism and Tall’s grumpy pragmatism balance one another perfectly, making them both likable and amusing companions to spend time with. The cast of secondary characters, from mischievous tricksters to eccentric villagers, adds even more personality to the world.

Visually, the game is a treat. The hand-drawn environments are richly detailed, with forests, swamps, mountains, and mythic locales brought to life in a whimsical, almost storybook style. The color palette is earthy yet vibrant, evoking a sense of myth and folklore while remaining playful. Animations, though not overly complex, contain small expressive flourishes that enhance the mood, and character designs are exaggerated in ways that emphasize their personalities. The visual direction ensures that each location feels distinct and that the game is consistently engaging to look at, even during slower stretches of exploration.

The gameplay sticks closely to the traditions of the genre, focusing on exploration, dialogue, and puzzle-solving. Most puzzles revolve around combining inventory items, interpreting clues from conversations, or experimenting with unusual interactions in the environment. At their best, the puzzles are clever and rewarding, pushing players to think laterally without feeling unfair. However, some solutions lean heavily on whimsical logic that may not be immediately intuitive, which can create moments of trial and error. Fortunately, the game includes a hint system that prevents progress from stalling entirely, though puzzle purists may choose to avoid it.

Humor and writing play a huge role in keeping the experience enjoyable. The dialogue is filled with witty exchanges, tongue-in-cheek jokes, and situational comedy that emerges naturally from the personalities of the protagonists and the ridiculousness of their quest. While the game is not fully voice-acted, the written lines are sharp enough to carry the humor on their own. The playful tone ensures that even when puzzles become a little frustrating, the story and characters remain engaging enough to encourage perseverance.

In terms of technical performance, tiny & Tall: Gleipnir – Part One is smooth and accessible. It runs well on modest systems, with no significant bugs or crashes to detract from the experience. The interface is straightforward, with intuitive controls for exploring, selecting items, and interacting with objects in the environment. While there are minor issues like unclear hotspots or occasional translation quirks, these are relatively small drawbacks in an otherwise polished presentation.

The game’s pacing is steady, offering a mix of exploration, puzzle-solving, and narrative moments that prevent monotony. Some players may find the overall length a little shorter than they would prefer, as the adventure comes to a close just as it feels like the characters are hitting their stride. However, the compact design also ensures that the story does not overstay its welcome, and it leaves room for anticipation of future installments.

Overall, tiny & Tall: Gleipnir – Part One succeeds in delivering a whimsical, funny, and visually striking adventure that pays homage to the point-and-click classics while injecting its own unique personality. Its blend of Norse mythology with absurd humor creates a memorable backdrop, and its mismatched duo of heroes are endearing enough to carry the experience. Though it has a few rough edges in puzzle design and pacing, it remains a highly enjoyable game for fans of the genre and anyone who appreciates a lighthearted, story-driven journey. It’s a strong beginning that leaves players eager to see where the series will go next.

Asıl hikayenin sadece üçte birini bu oyunda görebiliyoruz, kalan kısmını herhalde iki ayrı bölüm olarak planlamışlar ancak bu bölümün 2018'de piyasaya çıktığını düşünecek olursak... Herhalde hiçbir zaman gelmeyecekler. Kısacası evet, oyunu öneriyorum ancak "şartlı" öneriyorum, hikayenin tamamlanmayacağını bilerek indirimde satın almanız mantıklı olacaktır.

Oyunun içeriğine gelecek olursak... Bu bir cartoon Point & Click Adventure. Hikaye İskandinav mitolojisine dayanıyor, merkezinde kendilerini çevreleyen dünya ile alakasız görünen iki sevimli karakter var. Bulmacalar genel olarak çok tatmin edici. Oyunda bulmacalar konusunda muğlak biçimde aldığınız ipuçları gayet güzel düşünülmüş, oyunun sürükleyiciliğini bozmuyor (tabii olayın etik tarafını es geçip komple bulmaca çözümlerini de alabilirsiniz ama bu durumda oyuna neden para verdiğinizi sorgulamanızı öneririm). Son bölümde katılan absürd mizah etkisi pek hoşuma gitmedi ancak bunun dışında bana nedense Simon The Sorcerer'ı anımsatan, güzel, sürükleyici bir adventure oyunu var karşımızda.

Oyunun müzikleri ve görselleri çok güzel, seslendirme ise yok. Alışmakta ilk başta zorlandım ama daha sonra aramadım diyebilirim. Her neyse, devamının gelmeyeceğini ve yarım kalacağını bilerek indirimdeyken satın almanızı önereceğim bir oyun.

tiny & Tall: Gleipnir is a delightful adventure game. It took me a long time to get into it because the pacing doesn't make it easy to jump in. The game has a quiet, dream-like quality that sets it apart from your usual crowd-pleasing comedy adventure game. There is comedy here, but it's funny because the main characters get themselves into amusing situations and react accordingly, not because everyone you meet is trying to be a comedian. It feels classy and understated, which is a nice change when you are in the mood.

The puzzle solutions are also logical, within the context of a fantasy world where magic is real. The tools you find do more or less what you would expect them to do. What makes the puzzles sometimes frustrating is that there is no reveal hotspot button, and the interactive objects are painted no differently to the rest of the background. On top of that, some interactive objects (including characters) only appear on the second or third time you visit a location, without any hint to lead you back there to check. This would normally be an egregious failing for an adventure game, but because Gleipnir is so pretty, and there are so few locations and objects in the first place, it doesn't feel too bad.

Overall, it's a pleasure to play for adventure game fans. The art is fantastic and the music is really good too. The characters feel authentic and the story is fun. With just a bit of tweaking to help the puzzles become more discoverable, part two could be a classic.

[h1] Points positifs: [/h1]

- L'univers du titre à la sauce mythologie nordique
- Le scénario original et prenant
- L'humour omniprésent
- Le couple d'anti héros qui fait mouche
- Les graphismes magnifiques
- La bande-sonore sympathique
- L'accessibilité du titre et ses énigmes loufoques

[h1] Points négatifs: [/h1]

- Les bruitages minimalistes
- Un peu plus de difficulté dans les puzzles aurait été la bienvenue !
- La durée de vie (environ 5h00)

[h1] En conclusion... [/h1]

Rares sont les jeux d'aventures se situant dans l'univers de la mythologie nordique. A l'exception de quelques titres comme ''Heroïne's Quest'', ou ''The Frostrune'', on retrouve plutôt ce monde exploité dans des jeux d'action ou de stratégie. ''Tiny & Tall'' se glisse donc dans cette petite niche pour nous offrir un point'n click de bonne qualité.

Le monde d'Asgard est en danger ! Les Ases se sont réunis à la demande express d'Odin afin d'établir une stratégie pour contrer le Loup Fenrir. Si personne ne l'arrête, il finira par absorber le monde entier. Mais la Bête est si puissante que seule une chaîne magique saura l'entraver. C'est plein de détermination que le divin Thor confie cette mission à... deux petits forgerons sans histoire.

Les deux compères Tall et Tiny n'ont en effet pas l'envergure des héros. Tall, en particulier, est loin d'être motivé pour cette quête ne manquera pas de le rappeler sans cesse à son petit compagnon plein d'énergie qu'est Tiny. Le joueur contrôlera la plupart du temps ce dernier, et utilisera Tall à certaines occasions seulement. Très vite, on s'attache à ce couple de anti héros. Tiny est toujours prêt à tout, même s'il ne sait pas encore comment, et on l'adore pour ça. Cette ''partie 1'' sera consacrée à la quête des ingrédients nécessaires à la construction de la chaîne.

Visuellement, le jeu est de toute beauté. Pas étonnant quant on sait que le créateur est aussi dessinateur de bandes dessinées. On retrouve ici la patte de l'artiste, que ce soit dans les décors ou les personnages. Mais aussi dans les bonus, car au fur et à mesure de la progression, des véritables planches de BD se débloqueront, racontant l'histoire de bien belle manière. Et en français !

Le côté sonore est en revanche décevant. Il n'y a aucun doublage des répliques ; les bruitages sont minimalistes pour ne pas dire timides ; et la musique est certes réussie mais plutôt monotone. Dommage, cela réduit un peu le côté artistique de ce jeu.

D'un point de vue gameplay, on se trouve ici dans point'n click tout à fait traditionnel. On ramasse des objets, on les combine, on les utilise autre part et on passe à l'énigme suivante. Tout est relativement simple, à quelques exceptions près et surtout assez logiques (à une ou deux exception également). J'aurais aimé un puzzle un peu plus ardu pour mettre à l'épreuve ma matière grise, mais cet épisode 1 aura l'avantage d'être accessible à tous. Un système d'aide est astucieusement mis en place par l'intermédiaire de notre compagnon Tall. Il suffit de le questionner pour récolter quelques indices voire la solution d'un puzzle.

Il faudra 5 heures environ pour en venir à bout, ce qui est plutôt court. Cependant, il est indéniable que j'attends avec impatience le prochain épisode car la qualité est bien présente ! >> 16/20
